Title: O Estrangeiro
Author: Albert Camus
My Review:
Um verdadeiro exemplo da infelicidade da racionalidade.
A aceitação extrema pela ordem das coisas.
A indiferença ao que todo o ser humano não consegue ser indiferente.

O despertar efusivo perante algo no qual não se acredita, é o significado do poder da esperança, da luz e da vontade de sermos melhores, de evoluirmos, e de viver uma boa vida, mesmo quando não a conseguimos classificar como boa.

O seu destino trágico que só lhe pode dar conforto quando totalmente se aceita a vida que se teve, mesmo que por mais desgraçada que possa ter sido.
Porque só aceitaria ter outra vida se fosse "Uma vida onde me pudesse lembrar desta vida"

Quero tanto viver a vida depois desta leitura como o sol me quer aquecer nesta tarde.

Brilhante Albert Camus 🙏

Title: A Farça
Author: Raul Brandão
My Review:
- The story of a family that is extremely poor in monetary terms and struggles countless times for a better life. And yet, they maintain the honor and dignity of staying true to themselves, to the point of sacrificing opportunities they have always dreamed of for the sake of truth and honor.

- A mother who accepts everything, humiliation, defamation, and insults to her person so that her daughter may have even a little more chance of success than she did. A mother who perhaps tried too hard to be a good mother, and who inevitably failed.

- A woman who consciously forgot to love herself is what I see in this “old woman” beautifully described by Raul Brandão.

- Poverty and dignity, even in the face of the state in which we feel most insignificant and devalued, are concepts that most of us think about less and less these days, as they become increasingly distant from us. But it is essential to know that they exist and what they are in their crudest and harshest sense, and that is why, more than ever, I recommend this book to help us understand that we are never as bad as we force ourselves to feel.
